paragraphs.paragraph: The Prophetic Vision and Arrival in Jerusalem
paragraphs.title: The Prophetic Vision and Arrival in Jerusalem

easy.explanation: Ezekiel says, “I sat in mine house.”
easy.q: Where was Ezekiel sitting at the beginning of the vision?

easy.explanation: The elders of Judah sat before him.
The spirit brought Ezekiel to Jerusalem in the visions of God.
easy.q: Where did the spirit bring Ezekiel in the visions of God?

medium.explanation: The spirit lifted Ezekiel between the earth and heaven and brought him to Jerusalem.
medium.q: What caused Ezekiel to be taken from his house to Jerusalem?

medium.explanation: From the loins downward was fire, and from the loins upward was brightness.
medium.q: How was the figure seen by Ezekiel described?

answers: A prophetic experience came upon Ezekiel
An elder placed a hand on Ezekiel
medium.explanation: The expression introduces the divine prophetic experience that Ezekiel received.
medium.q: What does the expression “the hand of the Lord God fell there upon me” indicate in this passage?

answers: It was a prophetic vision rather than an ordinary journey
It was a dream belonging to the elders
challenge.explanation: Ezekiel was lifted by the spirit and brought to Jerusalem in the visions of God.
challenge.q: What does Ezekiel’s movement from his house to Jerusalem show about the nature of the event?

answers: The glory of the God of Israel
challenge.explanation: The glory of the God of Israel appeared according to the vision Ezekiel had seen in the plain.
challenge.q: What detail connects Ezekiel’s vision in the plain with this vision in Jerusalem?

answers: To the door of the inner gate that looked toward the north
To the southern gate of the Temple
challenge.explanation: He was brought to the door of the inner gate facing north.
challenge.q: Where was Ezekiel brought in Jerusalem?

paragraphs.idea: The Prophetic Vision and Arrival in Jerusalem

paragraphs.paragraph: The Symbol of Jealousy and the Abominations in the Temple
paragraphs.title: The Symbol of Jealousy and the Abominations in the Temple

easy.explanation: The Lord told Ezekiel to lift up his eyes toward the north.
easy.q: Toward which direction was Ezekiel told to look?

easy.explanation: He saw the image of jealousy at the gate of the altar.
easy.q: What did Ezekiel see near the gate of the altar?

easy.explanation: The Lord said, “thou shalt see greater abominations.”
easy.q: What did the Lord say Ezekiel would see afterward?

answers: Northward at the gate of the altar
medium.explanation: The image stood northward at the gate of the altar.
medium.q: Where was the image of jealousy located?

answers: They brought the people closer to the Temple
They caused the Lord to go far from His sanctuary
medium.explanation: The Lord said the abominations were committed so that He should go far from His sanctuary.
medium.q: What result did the abominations have, according to the Lord?

medium.explanation: The word refers to acts that the Lord regards as detestable and sinful.
medium.q: In this passage, what does “abominations” mean?

answers: Both are connected with sinful worship in the Temple
Both describe Ezekiel’s journey through the wilderness
challenge.explanation: The image is presented as part of the abominable worship taking place near the Temple.
challenge.q: What connection exists between the image of jealousy and the later abominations?

answers: To reveal the first offense near the altar gate
To send him back to his house
challenge.explanation: Looking north revealed the image of jealousy, after which Ezekiel was promised further sights.
challenge.q: Why was Ezekiel told to look north before being shown further abominations?

answers: The vision moves from the Lord’s glory to the exposure of Temple abominations
The vision moves only from women to elders
The vision moves from the Temple to Ezekiel’s house
challenge.explanation: After the glory of God is shown, the vision exposes the sinful practices defiling the sanctuary.
challenge.q: What progression appears in these verses?

paragraphs.idea: The Symbol of Jealousy and the Abominations in the Temple

paragraphs.paragraph: The Hidden Chamber and the Elders’ Worship
paragraphs.title: The Hidden Chamber and the Elders’ Worship

easy.explanation: Ezekiel saw “a hole in the wall.”
easy.q: What did Ezekiel see in the wall?

easy.explanation: Seventy men of the ancients of the house of Israel stood there.
easy.q: How many elders stood before the images and idols?

easy.explanation: Every man had his censer in his hand.
easy.q: What did each of the elders hold?

answers: A door leading into the chamber
medium.explanation: After digging in the wall, Ezekiel saw a door.
medium.q: What did Ezekiel discover after digging in the wall?

medium.explanation: The walls showed creeping things, abominable beasts, and the idols of Israel.
medium.q: What was portrayed on the walls of the chamber?

answers: Private inner rooms filled with images
medium.explanation: The phrase refers to the hidden chambers where the elders practiced their idolatry.
medium.q: What does “the chambers of his imagery” describe in context?

answers: They work openly but are afraid
They act in darkness but think no one sees them
They pray in the Temple and seek forgiveness
challenge.explanation: They practice their worship in the dark and say, “the Lord seeth us not.”
challenge.q: What central contrast appears in the elders’ behavior?

answers: It is used to justify their secret worship
It describes their prayer to the Lord
It explains why Ezekiel is at home
challenge.explanation: The elders use this belief to excuse their hidden and idolatrous behavior.
challenge.q: How does the statement “the Lord hath forsaken the earth” relate to their actions?

answers: Jaazaniah the son of Shaphan stood among the seventy
All the women stood with the elders
Ezekiel was one of the elders
challenge.explanation: The passage specifically names Jaazaniah the son of Shaphan among the elders.
challenge.q: Which easily overlooked detail identifies one of the elders?

paragraphs.idea: The Hidden Chamber and the Elders’ Worship

easy.explanation: Ezekiel saw women sitting at the gate of the Lord’s house.
easy.q: Who was sitting at the northern gate?

easy.explanation: The women were weeping for Tammuz.
easy.q: For whom were the women weeping?

easy.explanation: The Lord said Ezekiel would see greater abominations than these.
easy.q: What did the Lord say Ezekiel would see next?

answers: At the northern gate of the Lord’s house
medium.explanation: They sat at the gate of the Lord’s house that was toward the north.

answers: It comes after the vision of the chamber and the elders
It comes before Ezekiel reaches Jerusalem
It takes place in Ezekiel’s house
medium.explanation: After seeing the hidden chamber and the elders, Ezekiel is brought to the northern gate.
medium.q: How does the sight of the women fit into Ezekiel’s prophetic tour?

medium.explanation: The women were mourning and crying for Tammuz.
medium.q: What does “weeping” mean in this context?

answers: Each scene reveals an even greater abomination
The vision changes to an unrelated subject
The Lord returns to describing Ezekiel’s house
challenge.explanation: The Lord repeatedly announces that Ezekiel will see still greater abominations.
challenge.q: What does the Lord’s response after this sight reveal about the structure of the vision?

answers: It is another form of worship that is not worship of the Lord
It shows only the glory of the Lord
challenge.explanation: The mourning for Tammuz is another idolatrous practice revealed in the Temple area.
challenge.q: What connection exists between the women’s mourning and the previous scenes?

answers: It emphasizes that the abomination occurred near the holy place
It proves that they lived there
challenge.explanation: Their location shows that this idolatrous practice was taking place in the Temple’s vicinity.
challenge.q: Why is it important that the women were at the gate of the Lord’s house?

paragraphs.paragraph: Sun Worship and the Pronouncement of Judgment
paragraphs.title: Sun Worship and the Pronouncement of Judgment

easy.explanation: The passage says there were about five and twenty men.
easy.q: About how many men did Ezekiel see in the inner court?

easy.explanation: Their faces were toward the east.
easy.q: Toward which direction were the men facing?

easy.explanation: They worshipped the sun toward the east.

answers: Their faces were toward the Temple
Their backs were toward the Temple
They were sitting outside the Temple
medium.explanation: The passage says they had their backs toward the Temple of the Lord.
medium.q: What was the position of the men in relation to the Temple?

answers: Violence and provoking the Lord to anger
medium.explanation: The land was filled with violence, and the people had returned to provoke the Lord to anger.
medium.q: What other sins were mentioned along with sun worship?

medium.explanation: The phrase describes an additional insulting and provocative act against the Lord.
medium.q: What does the phrase “they put the branch to their nose” convey in context?

answers: The men turned their backs to the Temple while worshipping
They stood in the inner court
challenge.explanation: Turning their backs to the Temple emphasizes their rejection of the Lord’s worship.
challenge.q: What especially aggravates the description of the sun worship?

answers: The violence and abominations explain the severity of the judgment
The violence removes the need for judgment
There is no connection between the actions and the judgment
challenge.explanation: The Lord points to their violence and provocations before declaring that He will deal in fury.
challenge.q: How does verse 17 lead into the judgment announced in verse 18?

challenge.explanation: The Lord says, “though they cry in mine ears with a loud voice, yet will I not hear them.”
challenge.q: What would be the Lord’s response to their cries during the calamity?

paragraphs.idea: Sun Worship and the Pronouncement of Judgment
